   OLD TOWN LA VERNE BUSINESS IMPROVEMENT DISTIRICT
  MINUTES OF THE SPECIAL MEETING
  Monday, May 13, 2024

1.  WELCOME AND CALL TO ORDER

  Chairperson Walters called the meeting to order at 8:34 a.m. The following Board
  Members were present: Craig Walters, Marianne Stark, Mickey Rehm, Zuhey Espinoza
  and George Henderson. City Representatives present: Community Development Director
  Eric Scherer, Principal Planner Candice Bowcock, and Secretary Natalie Hiatt. Others
  present: Mia Valdez, Ken Valmonte, Fang Wang, Roy Cannizzo, and Francisco
  Ramirez.

2.  CALENDAR

  Annual Protest Hearing  Monday, 5/20 and 6/30 – 6:30pm
  Beer Walk  Saturday, 9/28 - 5pm-8:30pm

3.  APPROVAL OF THE MINUTES

  It was moved by Dr. Espinoza and seconded by Ms. Stark to approve the minutes of
  February 5, 2024, February 22, 2024, and April 1 2024. Motion carried by a 5-0 vote.

4.  NEW BUSINESS

  A.  Wine Walk Recap – Ms. Rehm provided the following figures: Ticket sales
  $50,545.01, costs $32,646, and estimated net profit $29,852.65. Ticket sales
  included 729 wine tasting tickets, 101 designated driver/food only tickets, and 77
  tickets given to the volunteers and sponsors.

  Ms. Rehm suggested cutting back on the number of bands next year to reduce
  costs. Mr. Scherer stated that Hal Fredrickson is not available to coordinate the
  bands next year.

  Mr. Walters stated that having one check-in at Mainiero worked well and there
  were plenty of volunteers from the Rotary and Women’s Club. Mr. Scherer added
  that the location of the portable restrooms worked, and they were utilized
  throughout the event.

  Mr. Walters recommended increasing the Food Tasting tickets to $45.00 next
  year.
 B.  Budget Review and Recommendation – Mr. Scherer stated that there might be a
  discrepancy with the total ticket revenue. Ms. Hiatt will review the totals and
  report back.

  Mr. Scherer reviewed the 2024/25 Budget Report with the group. He stated that at
  the end of the fiscal year it’s estimated they will have $160,000 in reserves. The
  report reflects a $30,000 transfer to the Association. The increase will help the
  Board catch up and fund a part-time employee to assist with the events. The
  Capital Outlay budget in the amount of $20,000 was previously budgeted to help
  fund the second phase of tree lights. Mr. Scherer stated that he thought the funds
  could be used for the purchase of brackets on the streetlights for decorative
  banners.

  Mr. Walters asked for an assessment of the condition of the existing tree lights.
  Mr. Scherer submitted a request to Public Works and has yet to receive an answer.
  He will follow up and report back.

  Ms. Scherer stated that the City Manager is in the process of preparing a request
  for proposal (RFP) for improvements in Old Town.

  It was moved by Mr. Henderson and seconded by Ms. Stark to recommend
  approval of the 2024/25 Budget to City Council. The motion carried by a 5-0
  vote.

  The Board also discussed the donation amount being given to the Rotary. It was
  moved by Ms. Rehm and seconded by Ms. Stark to approve a $2,000 donation to
  the Rotary. Motion carried by a 5-0 vote. Mr. Scherer stated that the check will be
  presented to the group at an upcoming City Council meeting.

  Mr. Scherer stated that it came to his attention that the process in which City
  Council approves the group’s budget was done backwards in the past. This year
  the first City Council meeting will approve the budget annual report and a
  presentation will be given by Mr. Scherer and Mr. Walters. This meeting is
  scheduled for Monday, May 20th at 6:30pm. At the second meeting there will be a
  protest hearing and a recap of the budget from Mr. Scherer. This meeting is
  scheduled for Monday, June 6th at 6:30pm.

C.  Café Wang Patio Recommendation – Mr. Scherer stated that the patio expansion
  expired in February and the Board approved an extension through May while a
  survey was performed by the Board.

  Mr. Henderson stated that a confidential survey was conducted for the businesses
  on D Street. He stated that 80% of the businesses were opposed to the patio
  expansion.
   Mr. Cannizzo spoke in opposition to the patio expansion but recommended that
  they keep it through the summer. He also recommended that after the patio is
  removed that the spaces be converted to handicap parking.

  Mr. Scherer explained that due to the design of D Street handicap parking would
  not work. He also stated that a resident contacted the City wanting the patio
  removed and the resident also spoke at a recent City Council meeting.

  Mr. Valmonte provided handout including data of the utilization of the patio. He
  stated that they tried to create a design everyone would enjoy.

  Dr. Zuhey asked for more information on the opposition that was provided during
  the survey. It was stated that parking or perception of lack of parking was the
  main opposition.

  Mr. Scherer stated that he intends to take the Sidewalk Dining policy back to City
  Council for review. The policy was originally drafted and approved in 2019. The
  current policy allows for each business to have two tables and four chairs at no
  fee. If more tables are requested there will be rental fee for the space being
  occupied. The business must also provide the proper insurance and ADA access.

  It was moved by Mr. Henderson and seconded by Ms. Stark to recommend to City
  Council the removal of Café Wang’s patio expansion at the end of the calendar
  year. Motion carried by a 3-2 vote (Dr. Espinoza and Mr. Walters voted no).

  Ms. Valdez volunteered to take the lead and organize the Beer Walk. Mr. Walters
  recommended she schedule a meeting soon. The Beer Walk is tentatively
  scheduled for Saturday, September 28th.

5.  CONTINUED BUSINESS

  A.  None

6.  COMMITTEE REPORTS/ UPDATES

  A. City Report (Eric Scherer): None
  B. University Report (Cindy Vallejo): Dr. Espinoza stated that the University welcomed
  the 19th President Dr. Pardis Mahdavi. The University recently participated in “Love
  La Verne Day” and they are hosting a community meeting on May 14th to discuss
  gate access on B Street. She stated that the University is working to be intentional and
  engaged with the community. The University is also developing a community
  calendar that can be easily accessed via a QR code.
  C. Marketing (Micky Rehm): None
  D. Chamber Report (Leah Skinner): None
  E. Social Media Update (Micky Rehm): None
  F. Financial Report: None
 7.  PUBLIC COMMENT (Any discussion or action on non-agendized items must be
  deferred to the following meeting, as required by California Brown Act Law)

  Mr. Cannizzo stated that he’s been in contact with Waste Management and Lisa O’Brien
  of the Public Works Department regarding a trash enclosure that was damaged behind his
  building. Ms. Bowcock will follow up with the matter and report back.

8.  ADJOURNMENT

  Meeting was adjourned at 9:48 a.m., the next regular meeting to be held on June 3, 2024
  at 8:30 a.m. at Café Wang – 2316 D Street, La Verne CA 91750.

  Respectively submitted,

  _____________________
  Natalie Hiatt

  MINUTES OF THE REGULAR MEETING
  Monday, June 3, 2024

1.  WELCOME AI{D CALL TO ORDER

  Chairperson Walters called the meeting to order at 8:33 a.m. The following Board
  Members were present: Craig Walters, Marianne Stark, and George Henderson. Not
  present: Mickey Rehm and Zuhey Espinoza. City Representatives present: Community
  Development Director Eric Scherer, Mayor Tim Hepburn, Council Member Steve
  Johnson, and Secretary Natalie Hiatt. Others present: Ken Valmonte, Fang Wang, Roy
  Cannizzo, Roberta Virgin, and Rick Sanders.

2.  CALENDAR

  Annual Protest Hearing - City Council  Monday, June 3'd - 6:30pm
  City Council Meeting - Caf6 Wang Patio  Monday, June 17th - 6:30pm
  University Dinner Crawl  Thursday, August 29th - 4-6pm
  Beer Walk  Tentative Date: Saturday, 9128 -
  5pm-8:30pm

3.  APPROVAL OF THE MINUTES

  It was moved by Mr. Henderson and seconded by Ms. Stark to approve the minutes of the
  May 13, 2024 meeting. Motion carried by a 3-0 vote.

4.  NEW BUSTNESS

  A.  University of La Verne Dinner Crawl - Cindy Vallejo of the University of La
  Verne announced that the Dinner Crawl event is returning on Thursday, August
  29s. Ms. Vallejo requested the BID provide a band at Mainiero Square.

  It was moved by Ms. Stark and seconded by Mr. Henderson to approve the
  expenditure. Motion carried by a 3-0 vote.

  B.  Beer Walk Update - Mia Valdez was not present to report on the Beer Walk
  meeting. More information will be emailed when it becomes available.

  C.  Summer Concerts at Mainiero - Mr. Walters asked if the Board was interested in
  hosting two concerts towards the end of summer.

  Mr. Scherer suggested staggering the dates so that it does not conflict with the
  Concert in the Park series at Heritage Park.
   lt was moved by Mr. Henderson and seconded by Ms. Stark to approve $1,000
  expenditure for two summer concerts to be held July 20th and August 17ft at 5pm.
  Motion carried by a 3-0 vote.

  D.  Cancellation of July 1.,2024 meeting - Mr. Walters stated that the next meeting
  will be cancelled due to lack of business.

5.  CONTINUED BUSINESS

  A.  None

6.  COMMITTEE REPORTS/ UPDATES

  A. City Report (Eric Scherer): Mr. Scherer stated that the Gold Line rail grinding is
  scheduled to end this week and construction is on schedule. Mr. Scherer recently
  toured the station platform. The University of La Verne is working on a plan to clean
  up the building visible from the platform. Mayor Hepburn stated that the City is
  working with Gold Line to create a walkway along Arrow Highway and clean up the
  weeds.
  B. University Report (Cindy Vallejo): Ms. Vallejo stated that students begin returning to
  campus next week and move in day is August l7th.
  C. Marketing (Micky Rehm): None
  D. Chamber Report (Leah Skinner): None
  E. Social Media Update (Micky Rehm): None
  F. Financial Report: None
7  PUBLIC COMMENT (Any discussion or action on non-agendized items must be
  deferred to the following meeting, as required by California Brown Act Law)

  Mr. Cannizzo commented on the patio structure at Caf6 Wang. He stated concerns that
  trwo of the voting board members are not business owners and the patio is not used
  enough.

  Mayor Hepbum and Mr. Johnson stated that they are present to support and for more
  information regarding the patio. Mr. Scherer stated that the City Council presentation will
  be on June l7m.

8.  ADJOURNMENT

  Meeting was adjourned at 9:06 a.m., the next regular meeting to be held on August 5,
  2024 at 8:30 a.m. atCafd Wang -2316 D Street, La Verne CA 91750.
